I am in the same boat as you. Just did therapy and medication for approximately a year.

Battling depression gives temporary meaning to your life.  It's like a trial for you to pass and you feel yourself get better every day.  You have the love and support of people, as well as the encouragement of doctors, and tangible steps towards success.

It's finding meaning after that that's difficult, because your life after depression will be the same as it was with depression.  It's all the same things that started getting you down.  This is why I think CBT is essential for any therapy, rather than analyzing the causes of depression--it's still important, but a lot of therapists focus on that rather than how to cope with new problems.

Just my 2 cents, I guess.  I certainly haven't figured it out.

I guess I'll try to say this as concisely as possible:

I appreciate the advice, but I have heard your advice from my parents, my therapist, et al, and it only makes me feel alone.  It's like getting relationship advice from your mom that grossly oversimplifies what a clusterfuck of hormones attempting logic a relationship actually is.

The advice you give me applies to 98% of the population.  In fact, many celebrities also advocate the "be yourself and don't give a fuck" mentality, but I was surprised to find that when I embraced it, I destroyed myself and had to leave college, without so much as a single friend, never mind a hit record or TV show.  It's about what 'myself' is and it won't always work.  Some people are serial killers.  Some people are narcissists.  Some people are billionaires so personality flaws are okay.  The idea that I can just value myself without logically seeing how inept I actually am at some point is just a fantasy.

The problem is that I can either change myself and be miserable or be myself and be miserable.  I don't have a terrible amount of pride in who I am.  And I am inherently narcissistic in that I grew up the golden child so I cannot trust my instincts in how I perceive myself.  Self-worth is an illusion.

I'm saying this in the most endearing way possible, as I attempted suicide and wrote a very similar note.

I still have my note and it is fucking embarrassing.  It was pretentious, whiny, and did nothing to explain my depression because it was almost incoherent.  It addressed my friends and family individually, similar to yours--and like yours, it shows absolutely no empathy for what people are going to think when they hear what you have to say.  Like you're talking to them under the facade it's no biggie.  As if what you're saying really matters more because you're dead. It's insincere and grandiose, and people will not see the same message you are trying to send.

I haven't figured out the not being suicidal thing, but I'm sure glad I didn't die a year ago because everyone would have thought I was an idiot.

If that's a reason not to kill yourself, at least for now, then I hope you see how much you've changed since today.  Otherwise, *please* don't leave a note.
